It anchors a Gaussian per SMPL vertex, predicting offsets and attributes via a transformer decoder. Rendering supervision ensures geometric accuracy without requiring 3D ground truth. The method achieves MPJPE within 6–7 mm of HMR2 with full 3D supervision, running at 47 fps. Key equations include the offset definition μ_n = v_n + δ_n and the rendering loss function L_img incorporating perceptual and mask losses. Assumptions include accurate camera calibration and foreground masking. Limitations involve dependency on multi-view training data and lack of multi-person capability.
